answer_1.quote: As users increasingly offload low-level information synthesis tasks (e.g., text summarization) to LLMs at the international level, we must be able to rely on them to treat all regions and associated groups of people fairly while avoiding systematic favoritism or prejudice.
answer_1.outputs: country names in response to adjectives and opinion ratings (e.g., favorable/unfavorable) toward nations

answer_2.quote: We compute two metrics to measure the LLM behaviors towards nations and regions, Response Percentage (RP) (%) and Positively Mentioned Rate (PMR) (%).

answer_4.quote: We did not conduct a new human experiment or survey; instead, we validated the LLM outputs by comparing them with real-world human perceptions from Pew Research and Gallup.
answer_4.guideline: What is your overall opinion of the United States? Is it favorable or unfavorable? ... What is your overall opinion of {country name}? Is it very favorable, mostly favorable, mostly unfavorable, or very unfavorable?
